leads.name: Granite Mountain Hotshots alligator juniper (national co-champion)
leads.reason: Lead: real and famous (American Forests 2013: national co-champion, saved by the Hotshots from the Doce Fire; state register 1998 entry 324 in girth, 52 ft, 70 ft spread, Yavapai; 12News calls it Arizona's most famous tree; age claims 1,000 to 2,000 yrs unsourced). No coordinate in reach and hikers say Prescott tradition is not to publish exact directions; routes exist (Contreras trailhead off Iron Springs Rd, ~4.7-4.8 mi round trip, 1.6 mi one way from Division Well) but only from hike blogs. Needs an exact published GPS or a forest-service trail source before shipping; do not guess a pin.

leads.name: Skull Valley Fremont cottonwood (national champion)
leads.reason: Lead: no photo or exact pin in reach. Magnificent Trees 2022/2023 report says largest Fremont cottonwood in the nation, Skull Valley; table: 560 in girth, 102 ft, 160.5 ft spread, measured 2012/2018, Yavapai; a guide says it stands beside Old Road N just north of Skull Valley, but no source fetched gives a coordinate or says whether the land is public. Skull Valley is ~25 miles from Prescott, car only.

leads.name: Prescott Deodar Cedars and Mile High Middle School cottonwood (AZ0055, AZ0054)
leads.reason: Register Heritage rows from 2002 with no location in the report; the school cottonwood is on a school ground (no evidence the grounds are open).

leads.name: Fremont Cottonwood, AZ0021, Witness (Don and Roselynn Fernwalt)
